claim: Current methodologies such as electron microscopy (EM) and super-resolution imaging techniques can provide precise localization of proteins but are limited to a small number of one-time observations with narrow spatial and molecular coverage.
source: Current methodologies, such as electron microscopy (EM) and super-resolution imaging techniques, can provide the precise localization of proteins, but are often limited to a small number of one-time observations with narrow spatial and molecular coverage.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods in the abstract, drawing on established knowledge about EM and super-resolution techniques.

claim: SubSynMAP generates probability distributions that reveal the functional range of proteins within the averaged synapse of a particular class.
source: SubSynMAP generates probability distributions for that reveal the functional range of proteins within the averaged synapse of a particular class.

claim: SubSynMAP enables the differentiation of closely juxtaposed proteins.

evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental scope in the abstract.

evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract, supported by data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Synapses are central to neural circuit function and dysfunction.
source: Synapses are central to neural circuit function and dysfunction, but their compositional diversity (there are hundreds of distinct protein species) and structural compactness (they average a single micron in size) have prevented their complete molecular analysis (Emes and Grant, 2012; Heuser and Reese, 1977; O'Rourke et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2008; Sheng et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Synapses have compositional diversity with hundreds of distinct protein species.
source: Synapses are central to neural circuit function and dysfunction, but their compositional diversity (there are hundreds of distinct protein species) and structural compactness (they average a single micron in size) have prevented their complete molecular analysis (Emes and Grant, 2012; Heuser and Reese, 1977; O'Rourke et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2008; Sheng et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: Synapses average a single micron in size.
source: Synapses are central to neural circuit function and dysfunction, but their compositional diversity (there are hundreds of distinct protein species) and structural compactness (they average a single micron in size) have prevented their complete molecular analysis (Emes and Grant, 2012; Heuser and Reese, 1977; O'Rourke et al., 2012; Chen et al., 2008; Sheng et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a factual statement about synapse size supported by citations.

evidence: This is stated with supporting citations about SIM capabilities.

claim: Fluorescence localization microscopy (PALM/STORM) can examine sub-cellular to single molecules at 10–50 nm resolution.

evidence: This is stated with supporting citations about PALM/STORM capabilities.

claim: Stimulated emission depletion microscopy (STED) can be used to visualize sub-cellular to sub-synaptic structures at 10–50 nm resolution.

claim: Traditional super-resolution methods are time consuming and struggle with both spatial coverage and molecular depth.

claim: SubSynMAP quantifies the nanometer distribution of multiplex proteins across large regions of the brain with synapse population specificity.
source: This current work introduces a new computational method (SubSynMAP: SUB-SYNaptic, Multiplexed Analysis of Proteins) that quantifies the nanometer distribution of multiplex proteins across large regions of the brain with synapse population specificity.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the method's capabilities.

claim: SubSynMAP is a combination of deconvolution array tomography (ATD), EM ratified computation synapse classification, and a new synapse alignment procedure.
source: SubSynMAP is a novel combination of previously developed volumetric super-resolution imaging of deconvolution array tomography (ATD) (Wang and Smith, 2012; Micheva and Smith, 2007), EM ratified computation synapse classification (Collman et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2014), and a new synapse alignment procedure.
evidence: This describes the components of the method with citations.

claim: ATD provides volumetric resolution of 100 nm by 100 nm by 50–70 nm.
source: ATD uses a combination of physical sectioning and deconvolved wide-field imaging to generate an unparalleled combination of acquisition speed, volumetric resolution (100 nm by 100 nm by 50–70 nm) and molecular multiplexing (Wang and Smith, 2012; Micheva and Smith, 2007).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations about ATD capabilities.

claim: EM verified algorithms can extract different classes of synapses with false positive rate of 5% and false negative rate of 12%.
source: These EM verified algorithms can be used to extract different classes of synapses (excitatory, inhibitory and their subclasses) at large numbers (>1 million) with low error rates (false positive 5%, false negative 12% – for more on antibody verification and error rates see 'Methods') (Wang et al., 2014; Allen et al., 2012; Hiu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations and references to methods.

claim: Proteins within presynaptic and post-synaptic compartments are spatially localized in relation to their function.

claim: Individual synapses vary greatly in their structure and molecular composition, but on average, the synapse remains an ordered structure with a specific distribution of protein populations.

evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

source: Traditional super-resolution or ultra-structural analysis routinely involves small sample sizes in terms of animals, synapse number and imaged volume.

claim: Over a half million synapses from 20 animals across two cortical layers were analyzed in this study.
source: In this study, over a half million synapses from 20 animals across two cortical layers were analyzed, creating an overall image that is more likely to reflect the reality of the synapses studied.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the study's scope.

claim: Layer 5 VGluT2 synapses only represent about eight percent of the total synapse population.
source: For example, Layer 5 VGluT2 synapses only represent about eight percent of the total synapse population
evidence: This is stated as an example of a rare synapse class.

claim: Of Layer 5 VGluT2 synapses, only about a quarter have FMRP in them.
source: and of that eight percent, only about a quarter have FMRP in them.
evidence: This is stated as further specification of a rare synapse subclass.

claim: A direct sample of 100 synapses in Layer 5 using traditional methods will yield, at most, two VGluT2 synapses with FMRP.
source: Thus, a direct sample of 100 synapses in Layer 5 using traditional methods will yield, at most, two VGluT2 synapses with FMRP, a quantity that is mostly anecdotal.
evidence: This is stated as a calculation demonstrating the limitation of traditional methods.

claim: 487 Layer 5 VGluT2 FMRP synapses were analyzed in this study.
source: In our study, we are able to analyze a total of 487 Layer 5 VGluT2 FMRP synapses, which provides a more robust measure of their structure.
evidence: This is stated as a description of the study's capability.

claim: Structural modification of synaptic proteins is hypothesized to be an integral part of most neurological diseases, yet there is little actual structural data supporting this.
source: Structural modification of synaptic proteins is hypothesized to be an integral part of most neurological diseases, yet there is little actual structural data supporting this.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current knowledge.

claim: The data gap regarding structural modifications in neurological diseases is caused by the potential diversity of synapse modifications, which requires large sample sizes.
source: This data gap is caused by the potential diversity of synapse modifications in neurological diseases, which requires large sample sizes to obtain significant numbers of similarly perturbed synapses.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the data gap.

claim: SubSynMAP can fill the data gap regarding structural modifications in neurological diseases.
source: Our method can fill this data gap.
evidence: This is stated as a capability of the method.

claim: Specific changes in protein locations mediated by FMRP loss within defined synapse classes were revealed in Fmr1 KO mice.
source: We demonstrated in Fmr1 KO mice that we are able to reveal specific changes in protein locations mediated by FMRP loss within defined synapse classes.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstration of the method's capability.

claim: FXR1P and FXR2P were localized within normal and diseased contexts, and their synapse localization was previously unknown.
source: We localized proteins (FXR1P and FXR2P), within normal and diseased contexts, whose synapse localization was previously unknown.
evidence: This is stated as a finding of the study.

claim: SubSynMAP can be generalized to a much wider array of cellular structures beyond synapse analysis.
source: Finally, the large-scale quantification of small, complex, stereotypically structured protein complexes is not just a problem in neuroscience, but in biology in general. SubSynMAP, while designed for synapse analysis, can be generalized to a much wider array of cellular structures and should provide a new level of analytical power for other disciplines such as immunology and cancer studies that require subcellular resolution investigations of large tissues.
evidence: This is stated as a potential application of the method.

claim: For Layer 4 cortical synapse axes, the mean is 677.04 nm, median is 704.50 nm, and standard deviation is 214.09.
source: For 102886 Layer 4 cortical synapse axes: mean = 677.04, median = 704.50, standard deviation = 214.09.
evidence: This is stated as a measurement from the dataset.

claim: For Layer 5 cortical synapse axes, the mean is 675.32 nm, median is 706.00 nm, and standard deviation is 216.18.
source: For 116592 Layer 5 cortical synapse axes: mean = 675.32 nm, median = 706.00 nm and standard deviation = 216.18.
evidence: This is stated as a measurement from the dataset.

claim: The synapse axis measurements are in line with published literature regarding the average size of a mouse cortical synapse.
source: All these numbers are in line with published literature regarding the average size of a mouse cortical synapse (Chen et al., 2008; Dani et al., 2010; Mineur et al., 2002; Chen et al., 2005; Tao-Cheng et al., 2014; Coleman et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated with supporting citations.

claim: The greater localization to the synaptic cleft region of GLAST as compared to GLT1 suggests that GLAST plays a more important role in the direct clearing of glutamate in the cleft.
